name: Testosterone (total)
rangeNote: For men, the app shows a reference position, not an alarm: 9.2–31.8 nmol/L (264–916 ng/dL) is the harmonised 2.5th–97.5th percentile range of healthy non-obese men aged 19–39, measured with assays calibrated to the CDC reference method. Levels tend to be lower in older men and with excess weight, and labs' own ranges differ by assay, so a lab's printed range takes priority. Guidelines advise a fasting morning sample and repeating a low result before drawing conclusions. No range is shown for women: normal values are much lower, vary with age, cycle and menopause, and depend on the assay (LC-MS/MS is the more accurate method at low levels).
summary: Testosterone is a sex hormone made mainly in the testes in men and, in much smaller amounts, in the ovaries and adrenal glands in women. The total test counts testosterone bound to proteins as well as the small part that is free.

high.meaning: A higher total testosterone means more of the hormone is circulating, either made by the body or taken from outside. It does not by itself show how much is active, because most of it is bound to SHBG (sex hormone-binding globulin), so a high SHBG can raise the total. In women, a raised level is one of the findings used when looking into conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome. Discuss unexpected results with your doctor.
commonCauses: Testosterone treatment (gels, injections, patches or pellets); gel can also transfer to another person by skin contact
HCG (human chorionic gonadotropin), which stimulates the testes to make testosterone
Clomiphene or similar medicines that raise the body's own production
High SHBG, which raises the total but not the free amount
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (an inherited adrenal condition)
Rarely, a testosterone-producing tumour of the ovary, adrenal gland or testis

low.meaning: A low total testosterone can be real or can come from a low SHBG, which lowers the total without lowering the free amount. A single low result is not enough on its own; guidelines recommend repeating a fasting morning sample and looking at symptoms and the cause. In women, low levels are expected after menopause or ovary removal. Discuss a repeated low result with your doctor.
commonCauses: Excess body fat, type 2 diabetes or metabolic syndrome
Acute illness, poor sleep or sleep apnoea, heavy alcohol use

Testosterone treatment, anabolic steroids or SARMs (selective androgen receptor modulators), which switch off the body's own production through LH (luteinising hormone) and FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone)
Low energy availability from very low food intake or very heavy training
Pituitary or hypothalamus conditions, high prolactin
Testicular conditions, such as Klinefelter syndrome, injury, infection or chemotherapy
Low SHBG, for example with obesity or insulin resistance
In women: menopause, ovary removal, and oral estrogens or contraceptive pills, which raise SHBG and lower the free amount
